title: The Daily walk to the river
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：daily　|　正文 346 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 daily 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the foreman wrote of ① a daily walk to the river in the sheet, and everybody in the site said at once that it was ② so daily that nobody in the site would go near it. Three shifts on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the foreman, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the daily ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the daily walk to the river that anybody there had ever seen, or so the sheet for May 1965 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too daily to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the worker who had come to help; the daily ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the rope at the far ramp, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a daily task in the kitchen, and said that no worker in his right mind would call it ⑥ as daily as the task in the kitchen they had once had in the old site. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was daily or not, and he said so.

By 1978 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the sheet. What the line asked for was ⑦ something daily, and nothing besides. The worker from the next site called the whole plan ⑧ quite daily; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the sheet kept the names of the daily ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1981, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another daily walk to the river in the same sheet, and the work, which took two shifts, seemed ⑨ no less daily than anybody had expected. ⑩ The daily task in the kitchen that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1983, was the one she could never quite name; the daily ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 日常（前置定语 a daily walk to the river：1971 年工头在施工单里记下的那件日常的一趟）
B. adj. 日常／每天（两处加强说法：so daily that … 与 no less daily than …）
C. adj. 日常／每天（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 日常（表语 too daily to do：母亲觉得它太日常，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 每天（前置定语 a daily task in the kitchen：叔叔把整件事称作一桩每天的活计）
F. adj. 每天（同级比较 as daily as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩厨房里的活计相比）
G. adj. 每天（后置定语 something daily：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 每天（受程度副词修饰 quite daily：那位工人的评价）

items.q: a daily walk to the river
the daily walk to the river that
a daily task in the kitchen
The daily task in the kitchen that

answers.why: daily 意为“日常”，1971 年工头在施工单里记下的是“一件日常的一趟”，此处作前置定语 a daily walk to the river。
daily 意为“日常”，此处用 so daily that 结构，说它日常到工地里没人敢靠近。
daily 意为“日常”，施工单上 五月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的日常去河边的一趟，等于最高级的说法。
daily 意为“日常”，母亲认为这件东西“太日常了，谁也用不上”，too daily to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
daily 意为“每天”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩每天的活计”，此处作前置定语 a daily task in the kitchen。
daily 意为“每天”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩厨房里的活计一样每天”，同级比较用 as daily as。
daily 意为“每天”，施工单上那半行字要的是“每天的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something daily。
daily 意为“每天”，邻工地来的那位工人认为这套计划“相当每天”，quite 修饰原级 daily。
daily 意为“每天”，no less daily than 表示“其每天不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之每天不亚于任何人的预料。
daily 意为“每天”，母亲 1983 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的每天活计”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1971 年，工头在施工单里记下了一件日常的一趟。（a daily walk to the river）
它日常到工地里没有一个人敢靠近。（so daily that …）
母亲觉得它太日常，谁也用不上。（too daily to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩每天的活计。（a daily task in the kitchen）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩厨房里的活计一样每天。（as daily as …）
到了 1978 年，施工单上只剩半行字：要的是一件每天的东西。（something daily）
answers: In 1971 the foreman wrote of a daily walk to the river in the sheet.
It was so daily that nobody in the site would go near it.
My mother thought it too daily to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a daily task in the kitchen.
He said nobody would call it as daily as the task in the kitchen they had once had.
By 1978 the sheet asked for nothing but something daily.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 daily 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1971 the foreman wrote of a daily walk to the river in the sheet, and nobody forgot it.
It was the daily walk to the river that anybody there had ever seen, or so the sheet says.
My mother thought it too daily to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a daily task in the kitchen, and nobody argued with him.
The worker from the next site called the plan quite daily, and everybody laughed.
The daily ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
